memoryVerse.text: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding;

source.details: Source ESV reads “Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding...” Prepared BSB uses “Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding;” Verify wording/excerpt and punctuation before publication. sourceFiles.note: Original 14-page OT19 lesson. Seven source Story Notes and all instructional/review questions retained; memory verse ESV excerpt separately preserved in provenance.

storyNotes.originalText: God told Jacob to RETURN to his father's land. God promised to be with him.
storyNotes.cleanText: God told Jacob to return to his father's land. God promised to be with him.

storyNotes.originalText: Esau headed to Jacob with 400 men. Jacob prayed, “Keep your PROMISE and save me from Esau!”
storyNotes.cleanText: Esau headed to Jacob with 400 men. Jacob prayed, “Keep your promise and save me from Esau!”

storyNotes.originalText: To stop Esau from attacking, Jacob sent his servants with a gift of many ANIMALS.
storyNotes.cleanText: To stop Esau from attacking, Jacob sent his servants with a gift of many animals.

storyNotes.originalText: A man WRESTLED Jacob all night long. Jacob would not let go until the man blessed him.
storyNotes.cleanText: A man wrestled Jacob all night long. Jacob would not let go until the man blessed him.

storyNotes.originalText: The man changed Jacob's NAME to Israel. He said, "You have struggled with God and won."
storyNotes.cleanText: The man changed Jacob's name to Israel. He said, "You have struggled with God and won."

storyNotes.originalText: That morning, Jacob said, "I have seen God FACE to face. But I'm still alive!"
storyNotes.cleanText: That morning, Jacob said, "I have seen God face to face. But I'm still alive!"

storyNotes.originalText: Jacob's family bowed before Esau. But Esau was no longer angry and GLAD to see them.
storyNotes.cleanText: Jacob's family bowed before Esau. But Esau was no longer angry and glad to see them.

questions.question: How many of you have ever wrestled with a parent or a friend?
questions.answer: Have the kids answer with a thumbs up or down.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Why was he living with his uncle in the first place?
questions.answer: He stole Esau’s blessing; Esau wanted to kill him.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Do you remember how many?
questions.answer: Twelve sons and a daughter.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: How did he know?
questions.answer: God told him.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did God promise to do?
questions.answer: Be with Jacob on his trip home.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did Jacob see?
questions.answer: Angels.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: When the messengers returned, they said, “Esau’s coming your way with…” what?
questions.answer: 400 men.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What was it?
questions.answer: God would be with him.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: However, do you think God ever forgets?
questions.answer: No.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did he hope would happen?
questions.answer: It would keep angry Esau from attacking.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What happened?
questions.answer: A mystery man wrestled with him.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Who was this stranger?
questions.answer: The lesson says the verses do not name the stranger.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: But did Jacob give up?
questions.answer: No.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: He said, “I won’t let go unless...” what?
questions.answer: The man blessed him.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What is your name?
questions.answer: Jacob.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What was that name?
questions.answer: Israel.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Now, do you remember why Jacob wouldn’t let the man go?
questions.answer: He wanted his blessing.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did he say?
questions.answer: I saw God face to face and I’m still alive.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Could God have out-wrestled Jacob if he wanted?
questions.answer: Of course.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did Jacob do as he came close to Esau?
questions.answer: He bowed seven times.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: And when he reached Jacob, what did he do?
questions.answer: He hugged and kissed his brother.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Pound him into dust?
questions.answer: No!
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Chop him in half with a sword?
questions.answer: No!
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Instead of attacking, what did Esau do?
questions.answer: He hugged and kissed his brother.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Do you remember Jacob’s prayer?
questions.answer: Keep my family and me safe from Esau!
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Did God answer Jacob’s prayer?
questions.answer: Yes.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: So how does the story of Jacob wrestling with God teach us, strengthen us, encourage us, or give us hope?
questions.answer: Open discussion; the lesson develops several applications.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: As Jacob wrestled the heavenly stranger, what did he do and say?
questions.answer: He held on and wouldn’t let go until the man blessed him.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What?
questions.answer: Contextual exclamation in a rhetorical teacher prompt.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Am I going to wrestle Jesus?
questions.answer: Of course not!
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: Who can tell us what it is?
questions.answer: Jesus died to save us from our sins, rose from the dead.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What does the Bible say will happen if we believe the good news of Jesus?
questions.answer: We’ll spend forever in God’s good kingdom.
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: After all, whose understanding of the world is greater: God’s or ours?
questions.answer: God’s!
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: After twenty years with Laban, what did God say to Jacob?
questions.answer: Return home; I’ll be with you
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did the messengers tell Jacob?
questions.answer: Esau is coming with 400 men
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did Jacob pray about?
questions.answer: That God would remember his promise and keep him safe from Esau
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What gift did Jacob give to Esau? Why?
questions.answer: Over 500 animals; he wanted to get on Esau’s good side
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What happened to Jacob the night before he met Esau?
questions.answer: A stranger wrestled him
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did the stranger do to Jacob as they wrestled?
questions.answer: Touched his hip and knocked it out of place
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did Jacob do as they wrestled?
questions.answer: Held on; wouldn’t let go until the stranger blessed him
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What new name did the stranger give to Jacob? What does it mean?
questions.answer: Israel; it means “struggles with God”
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What did Jacob say the next morning? What did Jacob name the place?
questions.answer: I saw God face to face and lived; Peniel, which means “face of God”
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

questions.question: What happened when Jacob met Esau?
questions.answer: Esau hugged him; was glad to see him
questions.notes: Original question retained from the lesson; contextual prompts may require teacher wording before use.

finishStory.markedParagraph: After twenty years with his uncle Laban, [Jacob] heard God tell him to return to his father's land. God promised to be with him. On the trip home, Jacob was afraid because his brother [Esau] was coming with four hundred men. Jacob [prayed] for help and sent his brother a gift of many [animals]. That night, after his family crossed the [river], a man [wrestled] with Jacob until morning. Jacob would not let go until he received a [blessing]. The man gave Jacob a new name: [Israel]. Jacob named the place [Peniel] because he said he had seen God face to face. The next day, Jacob bowed before Esau. Instead of attacking him, Esau ran to [hug] his brother.

reviewFlags.text: The original curriculum uses an ESV excerpt of Proverbs 3:5. Prepared verse activities propose the complete BSB verse. Confirm translation, exact wording, punctuation, and whether the full verse is desired.

The Bible passage calls Jacob’s opponent a man, records Jacob saying he saw God face to face, and the lesson notes the stranger’s exact identity is not specified. Avoid declaring an identification more certain than the source.
